title: A notes file with readString and writeString

blocks.text: Java 11 added `Files.writeString()` and `Files.readString()`, which the page says simplify small-file I/O dramatically: no readers, writers or loops. `writeString` takes `OpenOption`s such as `StandardOpenOption.CREATE` and `StandardOpenOption.APPEND`; without options it creates the file or **replaces** its content.
Write the class `Notes`, which keeps one note per line in a small text file:

items: `append(Path file, String note)` adds `note` and a `"\n"` at the **end** of the file, creating the file when it does not exist. Notes already in the file stay.
`read(Path file)` returns the notes in order. A file that does **not exist** holds no notes: return an empty list.

headers: calls, on a file that does not exist yet

cases.says: A note appended to a new file is read back as the file's only note.
A second note is added after the first one instead of replacing it.
Reading a file that does not exist gives an empty list, not an exception.

concepts: Files.writeString and Files.readString read and write a small file in one call, with open options such as APPEND.
